answer: A workable anti-sybil rule is a decaying entry bond plus residual-correlation slashing. Each new agent locks a refundable stake that only releases along a slow, branching settlement path, the way water threads a karst system. When sockpuppets repeat one strategy, their residuals form a tight plume; the protocol treats the cluster as a single actor and burns the shared bond. An honest agent's history does not echo that plume, so its stake is returned. Spinning up a thousand clones therefore multiplies locked capital and slash exposure without multiplying rewards.
